title: Backtested a momentum rotation strategy on AI Infra stocks (ARM, MRVL, etc.). +46% in 2.5 months, but need help stress-testing.
author: hialdu
selftext:
I've been seeing a lot of qualitative theses around AI infrastructure, memory, photonics, and networking. I wanted to know whether those ideas actually translated into performance.

I built a rules-based backtest that converted a public investor's recommendations into a systematic portfolio. Every published recommendation became a portfolio rebalance, and positions were adjusted only when the public thesis changed. No discretionary trades were added after the fact.

**Results (Apr 9 – Jun 23):**

* Return: **+46.07%**
* Trades: **42**
* Win Rate: **89.5%**
* Max Drawdown: **-14.8%**

The portfolio rotated through names such as **ARM, AAOI, MRVL, ONTO, NVTS, CAMT, and TSEM**, tracking changes in the underlying AI infrastructure thesis rather than simply buying and holding.

Obviously, this is **only a backtest**, not live performance, and the sample period is short. I'm not claiming this proves persistent alpha.

What I found useful was being able to inspect every rebalance and every simulated trade instead of judging an investment thesis from isolated screenshots or hindsight.

Has anyone here experimented with systematically converting qualitative research into a rules-based portfolio? I'd be interested in ideas for stress-testing this approach across different market regimes.
